source_records.title: Deligne’s numbered errata and convention changes
source_records.as_he_states: The letter proposes weaker assumptions at0.16.1.9,0.19.4.6/7,0.20.4.13; inserts local at0.19.8.3; reverses the universal-differential sign; rejects III4.3.6’s displayed completion formula.
source_records.plausible_today: Each is a separate edition-specific check; a sign convention is not a false theorem, and a suggested weakening is not an already established erratum.
source_records.state_of_art: Three exact checks are now complete. Printed0.16.1.9 p24 assumes noetherianity; its dimension equality extends without it because the faithful finite-module determinant trick makes B/Ann_B(M) integral over A/Ann_A(M), and integral extensions preserve dimension. Printed0.19.8.3 pp110–111 claims uniqueness among homomorphisms from a prime local ring: locality is essential, since every Z_(p) maps nonlocally to Q. Printed0.20.4.13(iv) p127 has the integral-closure hypothesis; localization gives Omega_B/A tensor Frac(B)=Omega_Frac(B)/Frac(A)=0 for an algebraic separable fraction extension, without integral closure. The0.20.4.6 sign is a convention requiring coherent propagation. The19.4.6–7 simplification proposals are not independently certified. Original EGAIII1,4.3.6 printedp133, has the alleged false equality. For A=Q[x,y]_(x,y), the prime (y−(exp(x)−1)) in Ahat contracts to0 and survives localization by A minus0, so Frac(A) tensor_A Ahat is not a field. The desired analytically-integral implies unibranch argument nevertheless works with the natural inclusion into Frac(Ahat). Full details are in proof_notes.md §11. The later published errata confirm the first three corrections and record the sign change, subject to the printed old/new-label transposition just described. Exact later errata: EGA IV4 Liste 3 de corrections, IV nos.6,9,12–14, printed pp.347–348 (1967). No.6 removes noetherianity from 0.16.1.9; no.9 inserts local in 0.19.8.3/4; nos.12–13 change the differential convention; no.14 removes integral closure in 0.20.4.13(iv) and supplies a denominator-clearing argument. The first p1/p2 instruction in no.12 itself has old/new labels reversed relative to the original p.125; its explicit tensor formula and no.13 determine the intended change. The 19.4.6–7 suggested proof simplifications remain separate bounded verification questions. The III4.3.6 equality is now verified false in the original print, while its conclusion is independently recovered using the natural injection.
source_records.why_open: The dated letter is an editorial check and ends with an explicit admission of an unfinished proof.
source_records.worth: Worth a line-level errata concordance; no mathematical novelty claim is justified by numbering alone.

title: Deligne’s deferred hard-Lefschetz proof request
as_he_states: In his letter of17October1966, Deligne says he will not attempt to prove the named théorème de Lefschetz vache that year and hopes Grothendieck finds someone who will. The sentence supplies no further hypotheses.
plausible_today: The historical sentence requests a proof of the named theorem without specifying a base field, coefficients or smoothness/projectivity hypotheses. The exact terminology in SGA7 XVIII5.2.2 identifies the standard hard-Lefschetz interpretation: for X smooth projective of pure dimension n over an algebraically closed field k, an ample invertible sheaf L, and a prime l different from char(k), cup product with c1(L)^i gives an isomorphism H^(n-i)(X,Q_l) -> H^(n+i)(X,Q_l(i)) for every i>=0. This precise statement is the later matched theorem, not a transcription of hypotheses from the letter.
state_of_art: SGA7II XVIII5.2.2 and5.2.2.1, printed pp281–282, use exactly the name Lefschetz vache for the cup-product isomorphisms and still conjecture the smooth case. The exposé is by N.Katz, expressly based on succinct Grothendieck notes (printed p254). Deligne, La conjecture de Weil II, Theorem4.1.1 and proof4.1.2–4.1.4, printed pp217–218, establish the stated smooth-projective Q_l theorem. The letter is dated17October1966; SGA7II was published1973; WeilII was received1June1979 and published in volume52(1980), with Numdam catalogue date28December1980. No exact first-circulation date is established. ClassB records establishment by another author relative to Grothendieck: Pierre Deligne, who also wrote the attached letter. Neither letter nor theorem is attributed to Grothendieck.
why_open: The source explicitly defers Deligne’s attempt for that year and asks that someone else undertake it. It states no mathematical reason for the deferral; the subsequent mention of convalescent EGA reading is not treated as a causal explanation.
worth: Worth retaining as a dated historical request with a later exact theorem match; the standard smooth-projective Q_l theorem is settled and does not warrant a new proof task here.

as_he_states:
Witness MP-SA23-099: Prove constructibility and hyperplane descent for the property that deletion of closed subsets of dimension≤m cannot disconnect X; the next witness corrects f to quasi-finite.

Witness MP-SA23-099: State the component-chain characterization for deletion of finite-image closed subsets. Source cue: Blass21: “a lemma that ought to appear in par.6 ... with Hartshorne’s theorem”.

Witness MP-SA23-099: Correct C_(m+1)→C_m by the actual image/quasi-finite hypotheses and formulate the broader connectedness statement. Source cue: Blass25: “error in the statement”; Blass30–31 expressly asks to generalize the connectedness formulation.

Witness MP-SA23-099: Generalize proper connectedness of all hyperplane sections to the stated dimension-sensitive connectedness conditions. Source cue: Blass30–31: asks the recipient to carry out the generalization as an exercise, or at least mention it as a remark.
plausible_today: Use quasi-finite f, or formulate all size conditions in image dimensions; distinguish generic from every hyperplane and properness.
state_of_art:
As of19November2026. This follows from classical Bertini irreducibility on each component and a chain of component intersections surviving the generic section. Stacks0G4C supplies the geometric-irreducibility input; this exact connectivity hypothesis is stronger than bare connectedness. Classical connectedness and EGAIV3 constructibility settle the component-chain ingredients. Searches of Bertini connectedness, Jouanolou, EGA and SGA did not identify the exact all-m relative C_m formulation with the draft’s quantifiers. The residual is that precise formulation and proof, not ordinary Bertini connectedness. For an integral source, EGA III1 Corollary4.3.7 and Remark4.3.8, printed133, gives the proper connectedness-specialization step over the normal dual projective space. Martinelli–Naranjo–Pirola Theorem1.1 supplies the irreducible projective case in any characteristic. The manuscript’s reducible case additionally uses its finite-image-deletion hypothesis; it is not a verbatim case of either cited theorem.

Established from the generic irreducibility theorem and the elementary component graph argument. The source prints f(X) in the definition of the exceptional family where f(Z) is necessary.

The image-dimension formulation follows by the component graph and dimension-drop argument; the unrestricted written formulation is false. The line “not valid if f quasi-finite” conflicts with the proposed fix and is retained as a likely missing “unless.”

Established Zariski connectedness/Stein factorization specialization, in the exact dominant-component setting. The inserted properness is included in the modern statement.

worth: Worth a focused reconstruction of the exact finite-type formulation, not an assertion that ordinary connectedness is open.

The exact scope of this tentative degree2 assertion remains a reading-and-hypothesis problem, not an accepted universal theorem.

as_he_states: Rewrite the end of the extension proof in terms of necessary and sufficient conditions, and first extract the stated corollary on locally free sheaves and relative Cartier divisors.

state_of_art: For the narrowed source question, with the following claim comparisons also documenting its asserted context: As of19November2026. Hartogs extension supplies uniqueness under the depth hypothesis. The unrestricted statement fails already for a one-member system: different effective fixed divisors give the same rational map to P^0. The later version is therefore a genuine correction, not just stylistic rewriting. EGA IV2 5.10.2 and5.10.5, printed114–116, proves the depth1/2 Hartogs criteria over locally noetherian schemes;6.3.1, printed138–139, compares flat-module depth with fiber depth. EGA IV3 11.3.7–8, printed135–136, supplies the finite-presentation relative regular-sequence mechanism used to remove noetherian hypotheses. \textbf{Lemme 3.} -- \textit{Il existe un nombre $c>0$ tel que, pour tout $n\geq1$, et tout $x\in T'_n$, l'indice de ramification de l'extension $K(x)/K$ soit $\geq c\cdot p^{nh}$.}

Admettons provisoirement ce lemme, et démontrons la prop. 8. Quitte à transformer $z$ par une homothétie, on peut supposer que $z\in T$ et $z\notin pT$. Pour tout $n\geq1$, l'image $z_n$ de $z$ dans $T/p^nT=T_n$ appartient à $T'_n$. Soit d'autre part $U=G\cdot z$ \textit{l'orbite} de $z$ par $G$. C'est une \textit{sous-variété analytique $p$-adique} de $T$ et son espace tangent au point $z$ est égal à $\mathfrak g\cdot z$ (cf. par exemple [7], LG, p. 4.12). D'autre part, l'image $U_n$ de $U$ dans $T/p^nT$ est égale à $G\cdot z_n$, ensemble des conjugués de $z_n$. Mais, d'après le lemme 3, on a $\operatorname{Card}(G\cdot z_n)=[K(z_n):K]\geq c\cdot p^{nh}$. D'où

\textit{Reste à démontrer le lemme 3.} Soit $v$ la valuation de $\overline K$, normalisée de telle sorte que $v(p)=1$. Soit $c_1$ la borne inférieure des $v(a_n)$, pour $n<p^h$. D'après ce qui a été dit plus haut, on a $c_1>0$. Soit $\varphi:\mathbf R_+\to\mathbf R_+$ l'application donnée par la formule

Soit $c_4$ la valuation d'une uniformisante de $K$, et soit $e$ l'indice de ramification de $K(x)/K$. On a évidemment:
\[
v(x)\geq c_4/e.
\]

En comparant, on trouve $e\geq c\cdot p^{nh}$, avec $c=c_4/c_3$, ce qui démontre le lemme.
